content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Predict the effect of changing concentration, pressure, and temperature
Apply Le Chatelier's principle to industrial processes
allows us to predict how an equilibrium will respond to changes in conditions. This is essential for industrial chemists who want to maximise product yield.
When a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in conditions, the equilibrium will shift to oppose the change.
The system tries to "undo" or counteract any change made to it.
Adding more of something pushes the equilibrium away from it.
Only affects equilibria with different numbers of gas moles on each side.
$$\text{(4 moles of gas)} \qquad\qquad \text{(2 moles of gas)}$$
Increasing pressure shifts equilibrium to the right (2 moles NH₃) because the system opposes by reducing pressure (fewer gas particles).
If equal moles on both sides:
Pressure change has no effect on position.
Catalysts do NOT affect equilibrium position.
Catalyst speeds up both forward AND reverse reactions equally
But the position (ratio of products to reactants) is unchanged
Same final amounts, just reached more quickly
System opposes by reducing pressure → shifts to side with fewer moles
System opposes by absorbing heat → shifts to endothermic direction
System opposes by using up SO₂
Predict and explain the colour change when:
System opposes by reducing pressure → fewer gas moles
Explain why adding a catalyst does not increase the yield of products at equilibrium.
A catalyst increases the rate of both forward and reverse reactions equally
It lowers the activation energy for both directions by the same amount
Both reactions speed up by the same factor
The same ratio of products to reactants is reached
The only difference is that equilibrium is reached faster
Catalysts speed up reaching equilibrium but don't change position
Forgetting to count moles of gas for pressure effects
Only gas moles matter; if equal, pressure has no effect
Check the ΔH sign - negative = forward is exothermic
Predict and explain the effect of:
For the Haber process: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) ΔH = -92 kJ/mol
Predict and explain the effect on equilibrium position of:
The equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g) involves colourless N₂O₄ and brown NO₂. The forward reaction is endothermic.
a) What colour change would you see if the temperature was decreased? (2 marks)
b) Explain your answer using Le Chatelier's principle. (2 marks)
Explain why removing a product shifts equilibrium to the right. (3 marks)
When equilibrium is disturbed, the system shifts to oppose the change
Change in equilibrium position to favour products or reactants
The relative amounts of products and reactants
Adding substance shifts equilibrium away from it
Remember: The system always tries to counteract the change made
